claim: Increasing the angular dispersion of arriving particles toward more horizontal trajectories enhances the shadowing effect, leading to faster column growth, larger separation between columns, and wider dispersion of column heights in thin-film growth by PECVD.
falsifier: The relationship can be tested by performing KMC simulations with controlled angular distribution parameters and measuring column morphology metrics such as height dispersion and separation.

conditions: simulated conditions for TiO2 and ZnO thin films using kinetic Monte Carlo method
substrate temperature corresponding to diffusion parameters D0=3e3 nm2/s, Eb=0.08 eV (TiO2) or D0=3e2 nm2/s, Eb=0.09 eV (ZnO)
angular distribution parameter vn=0 (more dispersed) compared to vn=0.73 (isotropic)
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported KMC simulations of TiO2 and ZnO thin films under the specified growth conditions; transfer to other materials or deposition methods is unestablished.

title: Angular dispersion of arriving–shadowing effect, column growth mechanism
